info.title: CVX bundle delivery
info.description: Delivers the current CVX standalone bundle as a file, and reports what the current release is. Both endpoints are static files with fixed bodies: they accept no input, carry no CV content, and nothing a user writes ever reaches them. They always describe the newest release, so a GPT using them needs no changes when CVX ships a new version.

servers.description: Static GitHub Pages origin — a JSON file, not a service.

get.summary: Download the current CVX bundle as a file
get.description: Call before promising a CV. Returns the current CVX release as a downloadable file: a zip holding one self-contained JavaScript file. Unzip it, then run it with node. Needs no installation. Always serves the newest release, so nothing here changes when CVX ships.

openaiFileResponse.description: One entry: the zipped CVX bundle.

get.summary: Current CVX version and standalone bundle download URLs
get.description: Reports the current CVX version, the minimum Node version, and stable download URLs. Use it to check whether a bundle you already have is out of date, or to give the user a link. Under 1 KB. It does not deliver the bundle itself; use downloadCvxBundle for that.

bundles.description: Stable download URLs, one per variant. Always resolve to the newest release.

checksums.description: URL of SHA256SUMS.txt covering every published artifact

aiGuide.description: Raw URL of the assistant-facing guide
